Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine Methode, die eine beliebige interne Tabelle als Eingabe akzeptiert und versucht, numerische Spalten zu identifizieren, um deren Summen in einem Balkendiagramm mit `cl_gui_chart_engine_win` darzustellen. Verwenden Sie RTTI, um die Spalten dynamisch zu analysieren.
hint: Nutzen Sie `cl_abap_tabledescr` und `cl_abap_elemdescr` für RTTI und dynamischen Datenzugriff.
solution:
CLASS zcl_chart_rtti_dynamic DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_chart_data,
             label TYPE string,
             value TYPE p DECIMALS 2,
           END OF ty_chart_data.
    TYPES tt_chart_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_chart_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    DATA mo_chart_engine TYPE REF TO cl_gui_chart_engine_win.

    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_container TYPE REF TO cl_gui_container.
    METHODS display_dynamic_chart_rtti
      IMPORTING it_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_chart_rtti_dynamic IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    CREATE OBJECT mo_chart_engine
      EXPORTING
        parent = io_container.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD display_dynamic_chart_rtti.
    DATA: lt_labels TYPE string_table,
          lt_values TYPE p_table.

    DATA(lo_table_descr) = cl_abap_tabledescr=>describe_by_data( it_data ).
    DATA(lo_struct_descr) = CAST cl_abap_structdescr( lo_table_descr->get_table_line_type( ) ).
    DATA(lt_components) = lo_struct_descr->get_components( ).

    LOOP AT lt_components ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_component>).
      DATA(lo_elem_descr) = CAST cl_abap_elemdescr( <fs_component>-type ).
      IF lo_elem_descr->is_numeric( ) = abap_true.
        DATA(lv_sum) TYPE p DECIMALS 2.
        LOOP AT it_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_line>).
          ASSIGN COMPONENT <fs_component>-name OF STRUCTURE <fs_line> TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_value>).
          IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_value> IS ASSIGNED.
            lv_sum = lv_sum + <fs_value>.
          ENDIF.
        ENDLOOP.
        APPEND <fs_component>-name TO lt_labels.
        APPEND lv_sum TO lt_values.
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    mo_chart_engine->set_chart_type( mo_chart_engine->co_type_bar ).
    mo_chart_engine->set_data(
      EXPORTING
        labels = lt_labels
        values = lt_values
    ).
    mo_chart_engine->draw_chart( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Entfernen Sie aufeinanderfolgende Duplikate aus einer internen Tabelle basierend auf einem Schlüsselfeld. Beachten Sie, dass die Tabelle vorher sortiert werden muss.

CLASS zcl_delete_duplicates DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             key_field TYPE c LENGTH 1,
             value_field TYPE i,
           END OF ty_data.
    TYPES tt_data TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS remove_adjacent_duplicates
      IMPORTING
        it_data TYPE tt_data
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_unique_data) TYPE tt_data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delete_duplicates IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD remove_adjacent_duplicates.
    rt_unique_data = it_data.
    SORT rt_unique_data BY key_field. " Wichtig für ADJACENT DUPLICATES
    DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES FROM rt_unique_data COMPARING key_field.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_duplicates( ).
    DATA(lt_test_data) = VALUE zcl_delete_duplicates=>tt_data(
      ( key_field = 'A' value_field = 1 )
      ( key_field = 'A' value_field = 2 )
      ( key_field = 'B' value_field = 3 )
      ( key_field = 'A' value_field = 4 ) 
      ( key_field = 'B' value_field = 5 )
      ( key_field = 'B' value_field = 6 )
    ).

    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->remove_adjacent_duplicates( it_data = lt_test_data ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_result ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_result[ 1 ]-key_field exp = 'A' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_result[ 2 ]-key_field exp = 'B' ).

ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine neue interne Tabelle, die alle Einträge einer Quelltabelle enthält, außer denen, die in einer Liste von auszuschließenden IDs enthalten sind. Nutzen Sie dabei die moderne `FILTER`-Syntax.
hint: Verwenden Sie `FILTER #( ... EXCEPT IN ... WHERE ... )`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_filter_exclude DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_item,
             id    TYPE i,
             value TYPE string,
           END OF ty_item.
    TYPES tt_items TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_item WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS filter_out_items
      IMPORTING
        it_source_items TYPE tt_items
        it_exclude_ids  TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_filtered_items) TYPE tt_items.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_filter_exclude IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD filter_out_items.
    rt_filtered_items = FILTER #( it_source_items EXCEPT IN it_exclude_ids WHERE id = id ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_filter_exclusion FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_filter_exclusion.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_filter_exclude( ).
    DATA(lt_source) = VALUE zcl_filter_exclude=>tt_items(
      ( id = 1 value = 'Item A' )
      ( id = 2 value = 'Item B' )
      ( id = 3 value = 'Item C' )
      ( id = 4 value = 'Item D' )
    ).
    DATA(lt_exclude) = VALUE STANDARD TABLE OF i WITH EMPTY KEY( ( 2 ) ( 4 ) ).

    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->filter_out_items( it_source_items = lt_source it_exclude_ids = lt_exclude ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_result ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_result[ 1 ]-id exp = 1 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_result[ 2 ]-id exp = 3 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: `FILTER` ist eine deklarative und effiziente Methode, um interne Tabellen basierend auf Bedingungen zu filtern. Die `EXCEPT IN`-Klausel ermöglicht das einfache Ausschließen von Einträgen, die in einer anderen Tabelle oder einem Bereich definiert sind, ohne explizite Schleifen oder `DELETE`-Anweisungen.
keywords: DELETE, FILTER, Internal Table, Modern ABAP, Functional Programming

Instructions: Löschen Sie eine spezifische Zeile aus einer internen Tabelle basierend auf ihrem Index.
hint: Verwenden Sie `DELETE TABLE ... INDEX ...`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_delete_index DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_line,
             text TYPE string,
           END OF ty_line.
    TYPES tt_lines TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_line WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS delete_line_by_index
      IMPORTING
        it_lines TYPE tt_lines
        iv_index TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_modified_lines) TYPE tt_lines.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_delete_index IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD delete_line_by_index.
    rt_modified_lines = it_lines.
    DELETE TABLE rt_modified_lines INDEX iv_index.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_delete_by_index FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_delete_by_index.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_delete_index( ).
    DATA(lt_test_lines) = VALUE zcl_delete_index=>tt_lines(
      ( text = 'First line' )
      ( text = 'Second line' )
      ( text = 'Third line' )
    ).

    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->delete_line_by_index( it_lines = lt_test_lines iv_index = 2 ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_result ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_result[ 1 ]-text exp = 'First line' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_result[ 2 ]-text exp = 'Third line' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: `DELETE TABLE ... INDEX` ist eine direkte Methode, um eine Zeile aus einer internen Tabelle zu entfernen, wenn der genaue Index der zu löschenden Zeile bekannt ist. Dies ist besonders nützlich bei Tabellen mit Zeilenindexzugriff.
keywords: DELETE, Internal Table, Index

Instructions: Deklarieren Sie eine Klasse als Freund einer anderen Klasse, um Zugriff auf deren private Komponenten zu ermöglichen.
hint: Verwenden Sie `FRIENDS` in der `CLASS ... DEFINITION` der Klasse, die den Zugriff gewährt.
solution:
CLASS lcl_target DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor.
    METHODS get_public_data RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_private_data TYPE string VALUE 'Private Data'.
    METHODS get_private_data RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
    FRIENDS lcl_friend. " Deklariere lcl_friend als Freund
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_friend DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_target TYPE REF TO lcl_target.
    METHODS access_target_private_data RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_target TYPE REF TO lcl_target.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_target IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_public_data.
    rv_data = 'Public Data'.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_private_data.
    rv_data = mv_private_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_friend IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_target = io_target.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD access_target_private_data.
    " Zugriff auf private Komponente von lcl_target
    rv_data = mo_target->mv_private_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_friend_access FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_friend_access.
    DATA(lo_target) = NEW lcl_target( ).
    DATA(lo_friend) = NEW lcl_friend( lo_target ).

    DATA(lv_private_data) = lo_friend->access_target_private_data( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_private_data exp = 'Private Data' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `FRIENDS`-Beziehung ermöglicht einen kontrollierten Zugriff auf private und protected Komponenten einer Klasse. Dies ist nützlich für eng gekoppelte Klassen, die interne Details voneinander kennen müssen, ohne die Kapselung für alle anderen Klassen aufzuheben.
keywords: FRIENDS, Class, Object Orientation, Private Access, Encapsulation

Instructions: Eine Klasse soll mehreren anderen Klassen Zugriff auf ihre privaten Komponenten gewähren.
hint: Listen Sie mehrere Freundklassen in der `FRIENDS`-Anweisung auf, getrennt durch Kommas oder Leerzeichen.
solution:
CLASS lcl_target_multi DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_secret_data TYPE string VALUE 'Top Secret'.
    FRIENDS lcl_friend_a, lcl_friend_b. " Mehrere Freunde
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_friend_a DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_target TYPE REF TO lcl_target_multi.
    METHODS get_secret_a RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_target TYPE REF TO lcl_target_multi.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_friend_b DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_target TYPE REF TO lcl_target_multi.
    METHODS get_secret_b RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_target TYPE REF TO lcl_target_multi.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_target_multi IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_friend_a IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_target = io_target.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_secret_a.
    rv_data = mo_target->mv_secret_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_friend_b IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_target = io_target.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_secret_b.
    rv_data = mo_target->mv_secret_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_multiple_friends FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_multiple_friends.
    DATA(lo_target) = NEW lcl_target_multi( ).
    DATA(lo_friend_a) = NEW lcl_friend_a( lo_target ).
    DATA(lo_friend_b) = NEW lcl_friend_b( lo_target ).

    DATA(lv_secret_a) = lo_friend_a->get_secret_a( ).
    DATA(lv_secret_b) = lo_friend_b->get_secret_b( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_secret_a exp = 'Top Secret' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_secret_b exp = 'Top Secret' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Mehrere Freundklassen können in einer einzigen `FRIENDS`-Anweisung deklariert werden. Dies ermöglicht es, spezifischen Klassen den Zugriff auf interne Details zu ermöglichen, ohne die Kapselung für alle anderen Klassen aufzuheben.
keywords: FRIENDS, Multiple Classes, Object Orientation, Access Control

Instructions: Eine lokale Klasse soll einer globalen Klasse Zugriff auf ihre privaten Komponenten gewähren. (Hinweis: Die globale Klasse muss bereits existieren oder simuliert werden).
hint: Verwenden Sie den Namen der globalen Klasse in der `FRIENDS`-Anweisung der lokalen Klasse.
solution:
" Annahme: ZCL_GLOBAL_FRIEND ist eine globale Klasse, die in SE24 definiert ist.
" CLASS ZCL_GLOBAL_FRIEND DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
"   PUBLIC SECTION.
"     METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_local_target TYPE REF TO lcl_local_target.
"     METHODS access_local_private_data RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
"   PRIVATE SECTION.
"     DATA mo_local_target TYPE REF TO lcl_local_target.
" ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_local_target DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_local_secret TYPE string VALUE 'Local Secret'.
    FRIENDS zcl_global_friend. " Globale Klasse als Freund
ENDCLASS.

" Simulation der globalen Freund-Klasse für dieses Beispiel
" In einem echten System wäre ZCL_GLOBAL_FRIEND eine eigenständige globale Klasse.
CLASS zcl_global_friend DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_local_target TYPE REF TO lcl_local_target.
    METHODS access_local_private_data RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_local_target TYPE REF TO lcl_local_target.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_local_target IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_global_friend IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_local_target = io_local_target.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD access_local_private_data.
    rv_data = mo_local_target->mv_local_secret.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_global_friend_access FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_global_friend_access.
    DATA(lo_local_target) = NEW lcl_local_target( ).
    DATA(lo_global_friend) = NEW zcl_global_friend( lo_local_target ).

    DATA(lv_secret) = lo_global_friend->access_local_private_data( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_secret exp = 'Local Secret' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `FRIENDS`-Beziehung funktioniert auch zwischen lokalen und globalen Klassen. Eine lokale Klasse kann eine globale Klasse als Freund deklarieren, um ihr Zugriff auf ihre privaten Komponenten zu gewähren. Dies erleichtert die Integration von lokalen Implementierungen in globale Architekturen.
keywords: FRIENDS, Global Class, Local Class, Object Orientation, Modularity

Instructions: Erklären Sie, warum eine Schnittstelle keine Freunde haben kann und wie man ähnliche Szenarien mit Klassen löst.
hint: Schnittstellen definieren nur Signaturen, keine Implementierungen oder private Komponenten.
solution:
CLASS zcl_interface_friend_expl DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_example_interface.
    METHODS get_private_data RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_private_data TYPE string VALUE 'Interface cannot have friends'.
    FRIENDS zcl_friend_of_implementing_class. " Eine Klasse kann Freunde haben
ENDCLASS.

INTERFACE if_example_interface.
  METHODS do_something.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_friend_of_implementing_class DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_target TYPE REF TO zcl_interface_friend_expl.
    METHODS access_implementing_class_private RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_target TYPE REF TO zcl_interface_friend_expl.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_interface_friend_expl IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD if_example_interface~do_something.
    " Implementierung der Schnittstellenmethode
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_private_data.
    rv_data = mv_private_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_friend_of_implementing_class IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_target = io_target.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD access_implementing_class_private.
    rv_data = mo_target->mv_private_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_interface_no_friends FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_interface_no_friends.
    DATA(lo_implementing_class) = NEW zcl_interface_friend_expl( ).
    DATA(lo_friend) = NEW zcl_friend_of_implementing_class( lo_implementing_class ).

    DATA(lv_data) = lo_friend->access_implementing_class_private( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_data exp = 'Interface cannot have friends' ).

    " Versuch, eine Schnittstelle als Freund zu deklarieren, würde zu einem Syntaxfehler führen.
    " Dies wird hier nicht direkt getestet, sondern durch die Erklärung verdeutlicht.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Schnittstellen definieren nur Signaturen und haben keine Implementierung oder private/protected Komponenten. Daher können sie keine Freunde haben, da es nichts gibt, worauf ein Freund zugreifen könnte. Die `FRIENDS`-Beziehung ist immer an eine Klasse gebunden. Wenn Zugriff auf interne Details einer Implementierung benötigt wird, muss die implementierende Klasse die Freundschaft deklarieren.
keywords: FRIENDS, Interface, Object Orientation, Limitation, Design Pattern

Instructions: Zeigen Sie, wie die `FRIENDS`-Beziehung in einer Vererbungshierarchie funktioniert und dass Freundschaften nicht vererbt werden.
hint: Eine Freundschaft wird nicht vererbt. Eine Unterklasse muss explizit als Freund deklariert werden, wenn sie Zugriff benötigt.
solution:
CLASS lcl_superclass DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor.
  PROTECTED SECTION.
    DATA mv_protected_data TYPE string VALUE 'Protected Superclass Data'.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_private_data TYPE string VALUE 'Private Superclass Data'.
    FRIENDS lcl_superclass_friend. " Nur dieser Freund hat Zugriff
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_subclass DEFINITION INHERITING FROM lcl_superclass.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_superclass_friend DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_target TYPE REF TO lcl_superclass.
    METHODS access_superclass_private RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_target TYPE REF TO lcl_superclass.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_superclass IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_subclass IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    super->constructor( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_superclass_friend IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_target = io_target.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD access_superclass_private.
    " Zugriff auf private Daten der Superklasse ist erlaubt
    rv_data = mo_target->mv_private_data.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_friends_inheritance FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_subclass_no_friend FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_friends_inheritance.
    DATA(lo_superclass) = NEW lcl_superclass( ).
    DATA(lo_friend) = NEW lcl_superclass_friend( lo_superclass ).

    DATA(lv_private_data) = lo_friend->access_superclass_private( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_private_data exp = 'Private Superclass Data' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_subclass_no_friend.
    DATA(lo_subclass) = NEW lcl_subclass( ).
    " Versuch, auf private Daten der Superklasse über die Unterklasse zuzugreifen, würde einen Syntaxfehler verursachen,
    " da die Unterklasse kein Freund der Superklasse ist.
    " DATA(lv_data) = lo_subclass->mv_private_data. " -> Syntaxfehler

    " Testen des Zugriffs auf protected Daten (erlaubt)
    DATA(lv_protected_data) = lo_subclass->mv_protected_data.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_protected_data exp = 'Protected Superclass Data' ).

    " Der eigentliche Test ist die Abwesenheit eines Syntaxfehlers im Code selbst,
    " wenn lcl_subclass nicht als Freund deklariert ist und versucht, auf private Daten zuzugreifen.
    " Hier wird nur bestätigt, dass protected Daten zugänglich sind.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `FRIENDS`-Beziehung ist nicht transitiv oder vererbbar. Das bedeutet, wenn Klasse A ein Freund von Klasse B ist, ist eine Unterklasse von A nicht automatisch ein Freund von B, und B ist nicht automatisch ein Freund einer Unterklasse von A. Jede Klasse, die Zugriff auf private oder protected Komponenten einer anderen Klasse benötigt, muss explizit als Freund deklariert werden.
keywords: FRIENDS, Inheritance, Object Orientation, Access Control, Subclass, Superclass

Instructions: Demonstrieren Sie eine bidirektionale Freundschaft zwischen zwei Klassen, bei der jede Klasse auf die privaten Komponenten der anderen zugreifen kann.
hint: Deklarieren Sie jede Klasse als Freund der anderen in ihrer jeweiligen Definition.
solution:
CLASS lcl_class_a DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_class_b TYPE REF TO lcl_class_b OPTIONAL.
    METHODS get_private_b RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_private_a TYPE string VALUE 'Private A Data'.
    DATA mo_class_b TYPE REF TO lcl_class_b.
    FRIENDS lcl_class_b. " lcl_class_b ist ein Freund von lcl_class_a
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_class_b DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_class_a TYPE REF TO lcl_class_a OPTIONAL.
    METHODS get_private_a RETURNING VALUE(rv_data) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_private_b TYPE string VALUE 'Private B Data'.
    DATA mo_class_a TYPE REF TO lcl_class_a.
    FRIENDS lcl_class_a. " lcl_class_a ist ein Freund von lcl_class_b
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_class_a IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_class_b = io_class_b.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_private_b.
    IF mo_class_b IS BOUND.
      rv_data = mo_class_b->mv_private_b.
    ELSE.
      rv_data = 'No B instance'.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_class_b IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_class_a = io_class_a.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_private_a.
    IF mo_class_a IS BOUND.
      rv_data = mo_class_a->mv_private_a.
    ELSE.
      rv_data = 'No A instance'.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_bidirectional_friends FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_bidirectional_friends.
    DATA(lo_a) = NEW lcl_class_a( ).
    DATA(lo_b) = NEW lcl_class_b( ).

    " Setze Referenzen für bidirektionalen Zugriff
    lo_a->constructor( lo_b ).
    lo_b->constructor( lo_a ).

    DATA(lv_data_from_a_to_b) = lo_a->get_private_b( ).
    DATA(lv_data_from_b_to_a) = lo_b->get_private_a( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_data_from_a_to_b exp = 'Private B Data' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_data_from_b_to_a exp = 'Private A Data' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Eine bidirektionale Freundschaft wird erreicht, indem jede Klasse die andere explizit in ihrer `FRIENDS`-Anweisung deklariert. Dies ermöglicht es beiden Klassen, auf die privaten und protected Komponenten der jeweils anderen zuzugreifen, was in Szenarien mit sehr enger Kopplung nützlich sein kann.
keywords: FRIENDS, Bidirectional, Object Orientation, Mutual Access, Coupled Classes

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine Klasse, die eine private Methode besitzt, und eine Freundklasse, die diese private Methode aufruft.
hint: Die Freundklasse kann private Methoden der befreundeten Klasse direkt aufrufen.
solution:
CLASS lcl_target_with_private_method DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS private_calculation RETURNING VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i.
    FRIENDS lcl_method_caller_friend.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_method_caller_friend DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING io_target TYPE REF TO lcl_target_with_private_method.
    METHODS call_private_method RETURNING VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mo_target TYPE REF TO lcl_target_with_private_method.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_target_with_private_method IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD private_calculation.
    rv_result = 10 + 5.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_method_caller_friend IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mo_target = io_target.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD call_private_method.
    rv_result = mo_target->private_calculation( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_private_method_access FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_private_method_access.
    DATA(lo_target) = NEW lcl_target_with_private_method( ).
    DATA(lo_friend) = NEW lcl_method_caller_friend( lo_target ).

    DATA(lv_result) = lo_friend->call_private_method( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = 15 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Freundklassen haben nicht nur Zugriff auf private Attribute, sondern auch auf private Methoden der befreundeten Klasse. Dies ermöglicht es, interne Logik zu kapseln, aber dennoch ausgewählten Partnerklassen den direkten Aufruf zu gestatten.
keywords: FRIENDS, Private Method, Object Orientation, Method Call, Encapsulation

Instructions: Verwenden Sie die `FRIENDS`-Beziehung, um eine Factory-Klasse zu implementieren, die Instanzen einer anderen Klasse mit Zugriff auf deren private Konstruktoren erstellt.
hint: Deklarieren Sie die Factory-Klasse als Freund der zu erstellenden Klasse, um den privaten Konstruktor aufrufen zu können.
solution:
CLASS lcl_product DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_id RETURNING VALUE(rv_id) TYPE string.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_id TYPE string.
    METHODS constructor IMPORTING iv_id TYPE string. " Privater Konstruktor
    FRIENDS lcl_product_factory. " Nur die Factory darf instanziieren
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_product_factory DEFINITION.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS create_product
      IMPORTING
        iv_id TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(ro_product) TYPE REF TO lcl_product.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_product IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mv_id = iv_id.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_id.
    rv_id = mv_id.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_product_factory IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD create_product.
    " Aufruf des privaten Konstruktors ist erlaubt, da lcl_product_factory ein Freund ist
    ro_product = NEW lcl_product( iv_id = iv_id ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_factory_friend FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_factory_friend.
    DATA(lo_product) = lcl_product_factory=>create_product( iv_id = 'PROD_001' ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = lo_product IS NOT BOUND ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_product->get_id( ) exp = 'PROD_001' ).

    " Versuch, lcl_product direkt zu instanziieren, würde einen Syntaxfehler verursachen:
    " DATA(lo_invalid_product) = NEW lcl_product( iv_id = 'INVALID' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `FRIENDS`-Beziehung ist ideal für die Implementierung des Factory-Musters, wenn der Konstruktor der zu erstellenden Klasse privat sein soll. Indem die Factory-Klasse als Freund deklariert wird, kann sie den privaten Konstruktor aufrufen und somit die Kontrolle über die Instanziierung der Produktklasse übernehmen, während die Kapselung des Konstruktors gewahrt bleibt.
keywords: FRIENDS, Factory Pattern, Object Orientation, Private Constructor, Instantiation Control

Instructions: Konvertieren Sie ein gegebenes Datum in das invertierte Datumsformat und formatieren Sie es anschließend in einem String-Template.
hint: Verwenden Sie `CONVERT DATE ... INTO INVERTED DATE` und String-Templates.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dte_convert_date DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS convert_and_format_date
      IMPORTING
        iv_date TYPE sy-datum
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_formatted_date) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dte_convert_date IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD convert_and_format_date.
    DATA: lv_inverted_date TYPE sy-datum.

    CONVERT DATE iv_date INTO INVERTED DATE lv_inverted_date.

    rv_formatted_date = |Original: { iv_date DATE = USER } | &&
                        |Invertiert: { lv_inverted_date DATE = USER }|.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_convert_date FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_convert_date.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_dte_convert_date( ).
    DATA(lv_date) = sy-datum. " Current date for testing

    DATA(lv_result) = lo_cut->convert_and_format_date( lv_date ).

    " Inverted date for current date is 99991231 - current_date
    DATA(lv_inverted_expected) TYPE sy-datum.
    CONVERT DATE lv_date INTO INVERTED DATE lv_inverted_expected.

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains(
      act = lv_result
      exp = |Original: { lv_date DATE = USER }|
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains(
      act = lv_result
      exp = |Invertiert: { lv_inverted_expected DATE = USER }|
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `CONVERT DATE ... INTO INVERTED DATE` Anweisung ist die Standardmethode zur Erzeugung eines invertierten Datums, das für bestimmte Sortier- oder Indexierungszwecke nützlich sein kann. String-Templates bieten eine moderne und lesbare Möglichkeit zur Formatierung von Ausgaben.
keywords: CONVERT, DATE, Inverted Date, String Templates, Formatting

    DATA(lt_summaries) = lo_cut->get_flight_summaries( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = lt_summaries OPTIONAL_MESSAGE = 'Table should not be initial if sflights has data' ).

END OF` definiert ist. Dies ist eine moderne Alternative zu expliziten `LOOP AT` und `APPEND` Anweisungen.
keywords: BEGIN OF, FOR, Internal Tables, sflights, Data Transformation

Instructions: Berechnen Sie die Summe von Mengen in verschiedenen Einheiten (z.B. KG und G) und konvertieren Sie diese in eine gemeinsame Einheit (z.B. KG) unter Verwendung von `CONVERT UNIT` und `REDUCE`.
hint: Kombinieren Sie `CONVERT UNIT` mit dem `REDUCE`-Operator.
solution:
CLASS zcl_mat_convert_reduce DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_quantity_item,
             value TYPE p LENGTH 16 DECIMALS 3,
             unit  TYPE meins,
           END OF ty_quantity_item.
    TYPES: ty_quantity_table TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_quantity_item WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS sum_quantities_in_kg
      IMPORTING
        it_quantities TYPE ty_quantity_table
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_total_kg) TYPE p LENGTH 16 DECIMALS 3.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_mat_convert_reduce IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD sum_quantities_in_kg.
    rv_total_kg = REDUCE #( 
      INIT total_kg TYPE p LENGTH 16 DECIMALS 3 VALUE 0
      FOR item IN it_quantities
      NEXT
        DATA(lv_converted_value) TYPE p LENGTH 16 DECIMALS 3.
        CONVERT UNIT item-unit
                INPUT item-value
                OUTPUT UNIT 'KG'
                OUTPUT lv_converted_value.
        total_kg = total_kg + lv_converted_value
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_sum_quantities FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_sum_quantities.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_mat_convert_reduce( ).
    DATA(lt_quantities) = VALUE zcl_mat_convert_reduce=>ty_quantity_table #(
      ( value = '1.5' unit = 'KG' )
      ( value = '500' unit = 'G'  )
      ( value = '2.0' unit = 'KG' )
    ).

    DATA(lv_total) = lo_cut->sum_quantities_in_kg( lt_quantities ).

    " Expected: 1.5 KG + 0.5 KG + 2.0 KG = 4.0 KG
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_total exp = '4.0' ).

    " Test with empty table
    DATA(lt_empty_quantities) = VALUE zcl_mat_convert_reduce=>ty_quantity_table #( ).
    DATA(lv_total_empty) = lo_cut->sum_quantities_in_kg( lt_empty_quantities ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_total_empty exp = '0.0' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `REDUCE`-Operator ist ein leistungsstarkes funktionales Konstrukt, um eine interne Tabelle zu aggregieren. In Kombination mit `CONVERT UNIT` innerhalb der `NEXT`-Anweisung können komplexe Berechnungen mit Einheitenumrechnung elegant und kompakt durchgeführt werden.
keywords: CONVERT, UNIT, REDUCE, Internal Tables, Aggregation, Math

Instructions: Konvertieren Sie eine UTC-Zeit in die lokale Zeitzone des Systems und geben Sie das Ergebnis aus.
hint: Verwenden Sie `CONVERT TIME STAMP ... INTO LOCAL TIME`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dte_convert_timestamp DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS convert_utc_to_local
      IMPORTING
        iv_utc_timestamp TYPE timestampl
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_local_time_str) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dte_convert_timestamp IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD convert_utc_to_local.
    DATA: lv_date TYPE sy-datum,
          lv_time TYPE sy-uzeit,
          lv_tzone TYPE sy-tzone.

    " Get current system time zone
    CALL FUNCTION 'GET_SYSTEM_TIMEZONE'
      IMPORTING
        tzone = lv_tzone.

    CONVERT TIME STAMP iv_utc_timestamp
            TIME ZONE lv_tzone
            INTO DATE lv_date
            TIME lv_time.

    rv_local_time_str = |Lokale Zeit: { lv_date DATE = USER } { lv_time TIME = USER } (Zeitzone: { lv_tzone })|.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_convert_timestamp FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_convert_timestamp.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_dte_convert_timestamp( ).
    " Example UTC timestamp: 2023-10-27 10:00:00 UTC
    DATA(lv_utc_timestamp) = '20231027100000'.

    DATA(lv_result) = lo_cut->convert_utc_to_local( lv_utc_timestamp ).

    " We can't assert exact time without knowing system timezone,
    " but we can check for format and presence of date/time.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_result exp = 'Lokale Zeit:' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_result exp = 'Zeitzone:' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lv_result ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `CONVERT TIME STAMP ... INTO LOCAL TIME` Anweisung ist essenziell für die korrekte Handhabung von Zeitstempeln über verschiedene Zeitzonen hinweg. Sie ermöglicht die Umrechnung eines universellen Zeitstempels in eine lokale Datums- und Zeitdarstellung, was für Anwendungen mit globalen Benutzern unerlässlich ist.
keywords: CONVERT, TIME STAMP, Local Time, UTC, Time Zones, Date/Time

Instructions: Filtern Sie eine interne Tabelle von Flugdaten (mit `BEGIN OF` Struktur) nach einem bestimmten Abflugort und speichern Sie die Ergebnisse in einer neuen internen Tabelle.
hint: Nutzen Sie `TYPES BEGIN OF ... END OF` und den `FILTER #()` Operator.
solution:
CLASS zcl_itb_filter_struct DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_data,
             carrid   TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid   TYPE s_conn_id,
             cityfrom TYPE s_from_cit,
             cityto   TYPE s_to_city,
           END OF ty_flight_data.
    TYPES: ty_flight_table TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS filter_flights_by_origin
      IMPORTING
        it_all_flights TYPE ty_flight_table
        iv_origin      TYPE s_from_cit
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_filtered_flights) TYPE ty_flight_table.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_itb_filter_struct IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD filter_flights_by_origin.
    rt_filtered_flights = FILTER #( it_all_flights WHERE cityfrom = iv_origin ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_filter_flights FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_filter_flights.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_itb_filter_struct( ).
    DATA(lt_all_flights) = VALUE zcl_itb_filter_struct=>ty_flight_table #(
      ( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' cityfrom = 'FRANKFURT' cityto = 'NEW YORK' )
      ( carrid = 'AA' connid = '0017' cityfrom = 'DALLAS'    cityto = 'LONDON'   )
      ( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0402' cityfrom = 'FRANKFURT' cityto = 'TOKYO'    )
    ).

    DATA(lt_filtered) = lo_cut->filter_flights_by_origin(
      it_all_flights = lt_all_flights
      iv_origin      = 'FRANKFURT'
    ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_filtered ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_filtered[ 1 ]-carrid exp = 'LH' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_filtered[ 2 ]-cityto exp = 'TOKYO' ).

    DATA(lt_no_match) = lo_cut->filter_flights_by_origin(
      it_all_flights = lt_all_flights
      iv_origin      = 'MUNICH'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = lt_no_match ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `FILTER #()` Operator bietet eine deklarative und effiziente Möglichkeit, interne Tabellen basierend auf bestimmten Kriterien zu filtern. In Kombination mit einer `BEGIN OF` definierten Struktur wird die Lesbarkeit und Wartbarkeit des Codes verbessert, da die Struktur der Daten klar definiert ist.
keywords: BEGIN OF, FILTER, Internal Tables, Data Filtering, Structure

Instructions: Konvertieren Sie einen String in ein sortierbares Format und vergleichen Sie zwei Strings basierend auf ihrer sortierbaren Repräsentation, um eine sprachunabhängige Sortierung zu ermöglichen.
hint: Verwenden Sie `CONVERT TEXT ... INTO SORTABLE TEXT`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_str_sortable_text DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS compare_strings_sortable
      IMPORTING
        iv_string1 TYPE string
        iv_string2 TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_comparison_result) TYPE i. " -1: s1 < s2, 0: s1 = s2, 1: s1 > s2
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_str_sortable_text IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD compare_strings_sortable.
    DATA: lv_sortable1 TYPE string,
          lv_sortable2 TYPE string.

    CONVERT TEXT iv_string1 INTO SORTABLE TEXT lv_sortable1.
    CONVERT TEXT iv_string2 INTO SORTABLE TEXT lv_sortable2.

    IF lv_sortable1 < lv_sortable2.
      rv_comparison_result = -1.
    ELSEIF lv_sortable1 = lv_sortable2.
      rv_comparison_result = 0.
    ELSE.
      rv_comparison_result = 1.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_compare_strings FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_compare_strings.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_str_sortable_text( ).

    " Test case 1: string1 < string2
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_cut->compare_strings_sortable( iv_string1 = 'Äpfel' iv_string2 = 'Birnen' )
      exp = -1
      msg = 'Äpfel should be less than Birnen'
    ).

    " Test case 2: string1 = string2
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_cut->compare_strings_sortable( iv_string1 = 'Test' iv_string2 = 'Test' )
      exp = 0
      msg = 'Test should be equal to Test'
    ).

    " Test case 3: string1 > string2
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_cut->compare_strings_sortable( iv_string1 = 'Zebra' iv_string2 = 'Apfel' )
      exp = 1
      msg = 'Zebra should be greater than Apfel'
    ).

    " Test case with special characters (locale-dependent sorting)
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_cut->compare_strings_sortable( iv_string1 = 'Müller' iv_string2 = 'Maier' )
      exp = 1
      msg = 'Müller should be greater than Maier (locale-aware)'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `CONVERT TEXT ... INTO SORTABLE TEXT` Anweisung erzeugt eine binäre Repräsentation eines Strings, die eine sprach- und locale-unabhängige Sortierung ermöglicht. Dies ist besonders nützlich für internationale Anwendungen, bei denen die Standard-String-Vergleiche zu unerwarteten Ergebnissen führen können.
keywords: CONVERT, TEXT, Sortable Text, String Comparison, Internationalization

Instructions: Erstellen Sie dynamisch eine interne Tabelle basierend auf einer vordefinierten Struktur, die mit `BEGIN OF` deklariert wurde, und fügen Sie Daten hinzu.
hint: Nutzen Sie `TYPES BEGIN OF ... END OF` und `CREATE DATA` mit `TYPE HANDLE`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dyn_create_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_dynamic_data,
             field1 TYPE string,
             field2 TYPE i,
           END OF ty_dynamic_data.
    TYPES: ty_dynamic_table TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_dynamic_data WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS create_and_fill_dynamic_table
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rr_data) TYPE REF TO data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dyn_create_table IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD create_and_fill_dynamic_table.
    DATA: lr_table_type TYPE REF TO cl_abap_tabledescr,
          lr_line_type  TYPE REF TO cl_abap_structdescr.

    " Get description for the structure type
    lr_line_type ?= cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_name( 'ZCL_DYN_CREATE_TABLE=>TY_DYNAMIC_DATA' ).

    " Create description for the table type
    lr_table_type = cl_abap_tabledescr=>create(
      p_line_type  = lr_line_type
      p_table_kind = cl_abap_tabledescr=>tablekind_std
      p_unique     = abap_false
    ).

    " Create dynamic internal table
    CREATE DATA rr_data TYPE HANDLE lr_table_type.

    " Fill data dynamically
    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lt_table> TYPE STANDARD TABLE.
    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <ls_line>  TYPE ty_dynamic_data.

    ASSIGN rr_data->* TO <lt_table>.

    APPEND INITIAL LINE TO <lt_table> ASSIGNING <ls_line>.
    <ls_line>-field1 = 'Dynamic Entry 1'.
    <ls_line>-field2 = 10.

    APPEND INITIAL LINE TO <lt_table> ASSIGNING <ls_line>.
    <ls_line>-field1 = 'Dynamic Entry 2'.
    <ls_line>-field2 = 20.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_dynamic_table_creation FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_dynamic_table_creation.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_dyn_create_table( ).
    DATA(lr_dynamic_table) = lo_cut->create_and_fill_dynamic_table( ).

    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lt_table> TYPE STANDARD TABLE.

Instructions: Konvertieren Sie einen Betrag von einer Währung in eine andere, unter Berücksichtigung eines Wechselkurses und eines Datums. (Vereinfacht, um die Syntax von `CONVERT CURRENCY` zu demonstrieren).
hint: Verwenden Sie `CONVERT CURRENCY`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_mat_convert_currency DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS convert_amount_to_target_currency
      IMPORTING
        iv_amount      TYPE bapi_curr
        iv_source_curr TYPE bapi_currcy
        iv_target_curr TYPE bapi_currcy
        iv_date        TYPE sy-datum
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_converted_amount) TYPE bapi_curr.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_mat_convert_currency IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD convert_amount_to_target_currency.
    " For demonstration, we'll use fixed exchange rate and factors.
    " In a real scenario, these would come from TCUR* tables.
    DATA: lv_rate TYPE f VALUE '1.10', " Example: 1 EUR = 1.10 USD
          lv_factor TYPE i VALUE 1,
          lv_gdatu TYPE sy-datum.

    " CONVERT CURRENCY requires a date for exchange rate determination
    lv_gdatu = iv_date.

    IF iv_source_curr = iv_target_curr.
      rv_converted_amount = iv_amount.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Simplified CONVERT CURRENCY statement
    " In a real system, this would involve reading TCURR, TCURF, TCURX etc.
    " and passing correct exchange rate, factor, and decimal shift.
    " Here, we simulate a direct conversion for syntax demo.
    IF iv_source_curr = 'EUR' AND iv_target_curr = 'USD'.
      rv_converted_amount = iv_amount * lv_rate.
    ELSEIF iv_source_curr = 'USD' AND iv_target_curr = 'EUR'.
      rv_converted_amount = iv_amount / lv_rate.
    ELSE.
      " Fallback or error handling for unsupported currencies
      rv_converted_amount = iv_amount.
    ENDIF.

    " The actual CONVERT CURRENCY statement (conceptual usage):
    " CONVERT CURRENCY iv_amount
    "         FROM iv_source_curr
    "         TO   iv_target_curr
    "         DATE lv_gdatu
    "         INTO rv_converted_amount
    "         RATE lv_rate
    "         FACTOR lv_factor.

  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_currency_conversion FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_currency_conversion.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_mat_convert_currency( ).
    DATA(lv_date) = sy-datum.

    " Test EUR to USD
    DATA(lv_converted_usd) = lo_cut->convert_amount_to_target_currency(
      iv_amount      = '100.00'
      iv_source_curr = 'EUR'
      iv_target_curr = 'USD'
      iv_date        = lv_date
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_converted_usd exp = '110.00' msg = 'EUR to USD conversion failed' ).

    " Test USD to EUR
    DATA(lv_converted_eur) = lo_cut->convert_amount_to_target_currency(
      iv_amount      = '110.00'
      iv_source_curr = 'USD'
      iv_target_curr = 'EUR'
      iv_date        = lv_date
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_converted_eur exp = '100.00' msg = 'USD to EUR conversion failed' ).

    " Test same currency
    DATA(lv_same_currency) = lo_cut->convert_amount_to_target_currency(
      iv_amount      = '50.00'
      iv_source_curr = 'EUR'
      iv_target_curr = 'EUR'
      iv_date        = lv_date
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_same_currency exp = '50.00' msg = 'Same currency conversion failed' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `CONVERT CURRENCY` Anweisung ist für die Umrechnung von Währungsbeträgen vorgesehen. Obwohl die vollständige Implementierung die Berücksichtigung von Wechselkursen, Umrechnungsfaktoren und Dezimalstellen aus den TCUR*-Tabellen erfordert, demonstriert dieses Beispiel die grundlegende Syntax und den Zweck der Anweisung. In der Praxis würde man hierfür oft Funktionsbausteine wie `CONVERT_TO_LOCAL_CURRENCY` oder `CONVERT_AMOUNT_TO_CURRENCY` verwenden, die die Komplexität der Tabellenlesung kapseln.
keywords: CONVERT, CURRENCY, Math, Exchange Rate, Währungsumrechnung

Instructions: Verwenden Sie `REDUCE` in Kombination mit einer `BEGIN OF` Struktur, um eine Aggregation über eine interne Tabelle durchzuführen, die sowohl numerische als auch String-Felder enthält.
hint: Nutzen Sie `REDUCE` mit einer `INIT`-Struktur, die mit `BEGIN OF` definiert ist.
solution:
CLASS zcl_itb_reduce_struct DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sales_item,
             product_id TYPE string,
             quantity   TYPE i,
             amount     TYPE p LENGTH 16 DECIMALS 2,
           END OF ty_sales_item.
    TYPES: ty_sales_table TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sales_item WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sales_summary,
             total_quantity TYPE i,
             total_amount   TYPE p LENGTH 16 DECIMALS 2,
             products_list  TYPE string,
           END OF ty_sales_summary.

    METHODS summarize_sales
      IMPORTING
        it_sales_data TYPE ty_sales_table
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rs_summary) TYPE ty_sales_summary.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_itb_reduce_struct IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD summarize_sales.
    rs_summary = REDUCE #( 
      INIT s_summary TYPE ty_sales_summary
           VALUE IS INITIAL
      FOR item IN it_sales_data
      NEXT
        s_summary-total_quantity = s_summary-total_quantity + item-quantity.
        s_summary-total_amount   = s_summary-total_amount + item-amount.
        IF s_summary-products_list IS INITIAL.
          s_summary-products_list = item-product_id.
        ELSE.
          s_summary-products_list = s_summary-products_list && ', ' && item-product_id.
        ENDIF
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_summarize_sales FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_summarize_sales.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_itb_reduce_struct( ).
    DATA(lt_sales) = VALUE zcl_itb_reduce_struct=>ty_sales_table #(
      ( product_id = 'A1' quantity = 2 amount = '10.50' )
      ( product_id = 'B2' quantity = 1 amount = '20.00' )
      ( product_id = 'A1' quantity = 3 amount = '15.50' )
    ).

    DATA(ls_summary) = lo_cut->summarize_sales( lt_sales ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_summary-total_quantity exp = 6 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_summary-total_amount exp = '46.00' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_summary-products_list exp = 'A1, B2, A1' ).

    " Test with empty table
    DATA(lt_empty_sales) = VALUE zcl_itb_reduce_struct=>ty_sales_table #( ).
    DATA(ls_empty_summary) = lo_cut->summarize_sales( lt_empty_sales ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_empty_summary-total_quantity exp = 0 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_empty_summary-total_amount exp = '0.00' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( act = ls_empty_summary-products_list ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `REDUCE`-Operator ist ideal für komplexe Aggregationen. Durch die Initialisierung mit einer `BEGIN OF` definierten Struktur (`INIT s_summary TYPE ty_sales_summary VALUE IS INITIAL`) kann der `REDUCE`-Operator mehrere aggregierte Werte (z.B. Summen, Listen) in einer einzigen Operation aufbauen, was den Code sehr kompakt und effizient macht.
keywords: BEGIN OF, REDUCE, Internal Tables, Aggregation, Structure, String Concatenation

Instructions: Parsen Sie einen JSON-String, der dynamische Schlüssel enthält, in eine Map-ähnliche Struktur (Hash-Tabelle).
hint: Nutzen Sie `cl_clb_parse_json=>parse` und `ASSIGN` an ein Feldsymbol vom Typ `STANDARD TABLE OF string WITH NON-UNIQUE KEY table_line` oder `SORTED TABLE` für Schlüssel-Wert-Paare.
solution:
CLASS zcl_json_parse_dynamic DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_entry,
             key   TYPE string,
             value TYPE string,
           END OF ty_entry.
    TYPES: tt_entries TYPE HASHED TABLE OF ty_entry WITH UNIQUE KEY key.
    METHODS parse_dynamic_json
      IMPORTING
        iv_json_input TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_entries) TYPE tt_entries.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_json_parse_dynamic IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD parse_dynamic_json.
    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <fs_data> TYPE REF TO data,
                   <fs_struct> TYPE any TABLE,
                   <fs_comp> TYPE any.
    DATA: lv_key TYPE string,
          lv_value TYPE string.

    TRY.
        <fs_data> = cl_clb_parse_json=>parse( iv_json_input ).
        ASSIGN <fs_data>->* TO <fs_struct>.

        IF sy-subrc = 0 AND <fs_struct> IS ASSIGNED.
          LOOP AT <fs_struct> ASSIGNING <fs_comp>.
            DATA(lo_struct_descr) = cl_abap_structdescr=>describe_by_data( <fs_comp> ).
            LOOP AT lo_struct_descr->get_components( ) INTO DATA(ls_component).
              ASSIGN COMPONENT ls_component-name OF STRUCTURE <fs_comp> TO FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_field_value>).
              IF sy-subrc = 0.
                lv_key = ls_component-name.
                lv_value = <fs_field_value>.
                INSERT VALUE ty_entry( key = lv_key value = lv_value ) INTO TABLE rt_entries.
              ENDIF.
            ENDLOOP.
          ENDLOOP.
        ENDIF.
      CATCH cx_sy_json_parser_error.
        " Handle error
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rtti_dynamic_table DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight_subset,
             carrid TYPE s_carr_id,
             connid TYPE s_conn_id,
           END OF ty_sflight_subset.

    METHODS create_and_fill_table
      IMPORTING
        iv_structure_name TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rr_dynamic_table) TYPE REF TO data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rtti_dynamic_table IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD create_and_fill_table.
    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <fs_table> TYPE STANDARD TABLE,
                   <fs_line>  TYPE any.

    TRY.
        DATA(lo_struct_descr) = cl_abap_structdescr=>describe_by_name( iv_structure_name ).
        DATA(lo_table_descr) = cl_abap_tabledescr=>create( p_line_type = lo_struct_descr ).

        CREATE DATA rr_dynamic_table TYPE HANDLE lo_table_descr.
        ASSIGN rr_dynamic_table->* TO <fs_table>.

        IF <fs_table> IS ASSIGNED.
          " Beispiel: Füllen mit Daten aus SFLIGHT
          SELECT carrid, connid FROM sflight INTO TABLE @DATA(lt_sflight_data) UP TO 2 ROWS.

          LOOP AT lt_sflight_data ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<fs_sflight_line>).
            CREATE DATA DATA(lr_new_line) TYPE HANDLE lo_struct_descr.
            ASSIGN lr_new_line->* TO <fs_line>.
            IF <fs_line> IS ASSIGNED.
              MOVE-CORRESPONDING <fs_sflight_line> TO <fs_line>.
              INSERT <fs_line> INTO TABLE <fs_table>.
            ENDIF.
          ENDLOOP.
        ENDIF.

      CATCH cx_sy_descr_param_error cx_sy_create_data_error.
        " Handle errors
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Überprüfen Sie, ob eine Methode in einer Klasse existiert und rufen Sie sie dynamisch auf.
hint: Nutzen Sie `cl_abap_classdescr=>describe_by_name` und `cl_abap_methdescr` für die Prüfung, und `CALL METHOD` für den dynamischen Aufruf.
solution:
CLASS zcl_rtti_dynamic_method DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS call_dynamic_method
      IMPORTING
        iv_class_name  TYPE string
        iv_method_name TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_success) TYPE abap_bool.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rtti_dynamic_method IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD call_dynamic_method.
    DATA: lo_class_descr TYPE REF TO cl_abap_classdescr,
          lo_method_descr TYPE REF TO cl_abap_methdescr,
          lo_object      TYPE REF TO object.

    TRY.
        lo_class_descr = cl_abap_classdescr=>describe_by_name( iv_class_name ).
        lo_method_descr = lo_class_descr->get_method_type( iv_method_name ).

        " Methode existiert, jetzt dynamisch aufrufen
        CREATE OBJECT lo_object TYPE (iv_class_name).
        CALL METHOD (lo_object)->(iv_method_name).
        rv_success = abap_true.

      CATCH cx_sy_descr_param_error.
        " Klasse oder Methode nicht gefunden
        rv_success = abap_false.
      CATCH cx_sy_dyn_call_error.
        " Fehler beim dynamischen Aufruf
        rv_success = abap_false.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

solution:
CLASS zcl_json_dynamic_writer DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_entry,
             key   TYPE string,
             value TYPE string,
           END OF ty_entry.
    TYPES: tt_entries TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_entry WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS create_dynamic_json
      IMPORTING
        it_entries TYPE tt_entries
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_json_string) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_json_dynamic_writer IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD create_dynamic_json.
    DATA(lo_json_writer) = cl_abap_conv_json_writer=>create(
                              pretty_print = abap_true
                              indent_level = 2 ).

    TRY.
        lo_json_writer->write_begin_object( ).
        LOOP AT it_entries INTO DATA(ls_entry).
          lo_json_writer->write_name( ls_entry-key ).
          lo_json_writer->write_value( ls_entry-value ).
        ENDLOOP.
        lo_json_writer->write_end_object( ).
        rv_json_string = lo_json_writer->get_json_string( ).

      CATCH cx_abap_conv_json_error.
        " Handle errors
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Gruppieren Sie Flüge nach Fluggesellschaft (`carrid`) und Verbindungsnummer (`connid`). Zählen Sie die Anzahl der Flüge pro Gruppe und geben Sie das Ergebnis zurück.

solution:
CLASS zcl_grp_002 DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             seatsocc TYPE sflight-seatsocc,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES ty_t_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_grouped_count,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid TYPE sflight-connid,
             count  TYPE i,
           END OF ty_grouped_count.
    TYPES ty_t_grouped_count TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_grouped_count WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_flight_counts_by_group
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_grouped_counts) TYPE ty_t_grouped_count.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_grp_002 IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_flight_counts_by_group.
    DATA lt_sflights TYPE ty_t_sflight.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsocc
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_flight) GROUP BY ( carrid = ls_flight-carrid connid = ls_flight-connid )
                                              INTO DATA(ls_group_key).
      APPEND VALUE ty_grouped_count( carrid = ls_group_key-carrid
                                     connid = ls_group_key-connid
                                     count  = GROUP SIZE ) TO rt_grouped_counts.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.

Instructions: Gruppieren Sie Flüge nach Fluggesellschaft (`carrid`) und berechnen Sie die Summe der belegten Sitze (`seatsocc`) pro Fluggesellschaft.
hint: Nutzen Sie `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY` und den `REDUCE` Operator für die Aggregation der Gruppenelemente.
solution:
CLASS zcl_grp_003 DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             seatsocc TYPE sflight-seatsocc,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES ty_t_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_grouped_seats,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             total_seats TYPE i,
           END OF ty_grouped_seats.
    TYPES ty_t_grouped_seats TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_grouped_seats WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_total_seats_by_carrier
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_grouped_seats) TYPE ty_t_grouped_seats.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_grp_003 IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_total_seats_by_carrier.
    DATA lt_sflights TYPE ty_t_sflight.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsocc
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_flight) GROUP BY ls_flight-carrid INTO DATA(ls_group_key).
      DATA(lv_total_seats) = REDUCE i( INIT sum = 0
                                        FOR ls_member IN GROUP ls_group_key
                                        NEXT sum = sum + ls_member-seatsocc ).
      APPEND VALUE ty_grouped_seats( carrid = ls_group_key-carrid
                                     total_seats = lv_total_seats ) TO rt_grouped_seats.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_total_seats FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_total_seats.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_grp_003( ).
    DATA(lt_grouped_seats) = lo_cut->get_total_seats_by_carrier( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lt_grouped_seats ).
    LOOP AT lt_grouped_seats INTO DATA(ls_seats).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( ls_seats-total_seats >= 0 ).
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die Kombination von `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY` mit dem `REDUCE` Operator innerhalb der Gruppenschleife ist ein sehr mächtiges und modernes Muster zur Aggregation von Daten. Es ermöglicht die Berechnung von Summen, Durchschnitten oder anderen Aggregaten auf eine deklarative und lesbare Weise, ohne manuelle Schleifen und Hilfsvariablen.
keywords: LOOP AT, GROUP BY, REDUCE, Data Aggregation, Internal Tables, Functional Programming

Instructions: Gruppieren Sie Flüge zuerst nach Fluggesellschaft (`carrid`) und dann innerhalb jeder Fluggesellschaft nach dem Abflugdatum (`fldate`). Geben Sie die hierarchisch gruppierten Daten zurück.
hint: Verwenden Sie verschachtelte `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY` Anweisungen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_grp_006 DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             seatsocc TYPE sflight-seatsocc,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES ty_t_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_date_group,
             fldate TYPE sflight-fldate,
             flights TYPE ty_t_sflight,
           END OF ty_date_group.
    TYPES ty_t_date_group TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_date_group WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_carrier_group,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             date_groups TYPE ty_t_date_group,
           END OF ty_carrier_group.
    TYPES ty_t_carrier_group TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_carrier_group WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_nested_grouped_flights
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_nested_groups) TYPE ty_t_carrier_group.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_grp_006 IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_nested_grouped_flights.
    DATA lt_sflights TYPE ty_t_sflight.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsocc
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_flight_carr) GROUP BY ls_flight_carr-carrid INTO DATA(ls_carrier_group_key).
      DATA ls_carrier_group TYPE ty_carrier_group.
      ls_carrier_group-carrid = ls_carrier_group_key-carrid.

      LOOP AT GROUP ls_carrier_group_key INTO DATA(ls_flight_date) GROUP BY ls_flight_date-fldate INTO DATA(ls_date_group_key).
        DATA ls_date_group TYPE ty_date_group.
        ls_date_group-fldate = ls_date_group_key-fldate.
        LOOP AT GROUP ls_date_group_key INTO DATA(ls_member).
          APPEND ls_member TO ls_date_group-flights.
        ENDLOOP.
        APPEND ls_date_group TO ls_carrier_group-date_groups.
      ENDLOOP.
      APPEND ls_carrier_group TO rt_nested_groups.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_nested_grouping FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_nested_grouping.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_grp_006( ).
    DATA(lt_nested_groups) = lo_cut->get_nested_grouped_flights( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lt_nested_groups ).
    LOOP AT lt_nested_groups INTO DATA(ls_carrier_group).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = ls_carrier_group-carrid ).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = ls_carrier_group-date_groups ).
      LOOP AT ls_carrier_group-date_groups INTO DATA(ls_date_group).
        cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = ls_date_group-fldate ).
        cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = ls_date_group-flights ).
      ENDLOOP.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connids TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight-connid WITH EMPTY KEY,
           END OF ty_carrier_conns.
    TYPES ty_t_carrier_conns TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_carrier_conns WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_carrier_with_sample_conns
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_carrier_conns) TYPE ty_t_carrier_conns.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_grp_007 IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_carrier_with_sample_conns.
    DATA lt_sflights TYPE ty_t_sflight.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsocc
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_flight) GROUP BY ls_flight-carrid INTO DATA(ls_group_key).
      DATA ls_carrier_conns TYPE ty_carrier_conns.
      ls_carrier_conns-carrid = ls_group_key-carrid.

      LOOP AT GROUP ls_group_key INTO DATA(ls_member) UP TO 3 ROWS.
        APPEND ls_member-connid TO ls_carrier_conns-connids.
      ENDLOOP.
      APPEND ls_carrier_conns TO rt_carrier_conns.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine neue interne Tabelle, die für jede Fluggesellschaft die Anzahl der Flüge und die Summe der Sitze enthält, unter Verwendung eines `FOR` Ausdrucks mit `GROUP BY`.
hint: Kombinieren Sie `FOR ... IN ... GROUP BY` mit `REDUCE` für die Aggregation.
solution:
CLASS zcl_grp_008 DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             seatsocc TYPE sflight-seatsocc,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES ty_t_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_carrier_summary,
             carrid      TYPE sflight-carrid,
             flight_count TYPE i,
             total_seats TYPE i,
           END OF ty_carrier_summary.
    TYPES ty_t_carrier_summary TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_carrier_summary WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_carrier_summary
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_summary) TYPE ty_t_carrier_summary.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_grp_008 IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_carrier_summary.
    DATA lt_sflights TYPE ty_t_sflight.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsocc
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    rt_summary = VALUE #( FOR GROUPS OF ls_flight IN lt_sflights GROUP BY ls_flight-carrid
                          ( carrid       = ls_flight-carrid
                            flight_count = GROUP SIZE
                            total_seats  = REDUCE i( INIT sum = 0
                                                     FOR ls_member IN GROUP ls_flight
                                                     NEXT sum = sum + ls_member-seatsocc ) ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_grp_008( ).
    DATA(lt_summary) = lo_cut->get_carrier_summary( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lt_summary ).
    LOOP AT lt_summary INTO DATA(ls_entry).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = ls_entry-carrid ).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( ls_entry-flight_count > 0 ).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( ls_entry-total_seats >= 0 ).
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die Kombination von `FOR GROUPS OF ... GROUP BY` mit `REDUCE` ist ein Paradebeispiel für moderne, funktionale ABAP-Programmierung. Sie ermöglicht die deklarative Erstellung aggregierter interner Tabellen in einer einzigen Anweisung, was den Code extrem kompakt, lesbar und wartbar macht. Dies ist wesentlich effizienter und eleganter als traditionelle Schleifen mit manuellen Aggregationen.
keywords: FOR, GROUP BY, REDUCE, Data Aggregation, Internal Tables, Functional Programming, Value Operator

Instructions: Gruppieren Sie Flüge nach Fluggesellschaft (`carrid`) und zählen Sie die Anzahl der Flüge pro Fluggesellschaft. Zeigen Sie die moderne Lösung mit `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY` und erwähnen Sie `COLLECT` als traditionelle Alternative.
hint: Fokus auf `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY` mit `GROUP SIZE`. `COLLECT` ist eine ältere Methode für ähnliche Aggregationen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_grp_010 DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_sflight,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             seatsocc TYPE sflight-seatsocc,
           END OF ty_sflight.
    TYPES ty_t_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_carrier_count,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             count  TYPE i,
           END OF ty_carrier_count.
    TYPES ty_t_carrier_count TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_carrier_count WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_carrier_flight_counts
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_counts) TYPE ty_t_carrier_count.

    METHODS get_carrier_flight_counts_collect
      RETURNING VALUE(rt_counts) TYPE ty_t_carrier_count.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_grp_010 IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_carrier_flight_counts.
    DATA lt_sflights TYPE ty_t_sflight.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsocc
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_flight) GROUP BY ls_flight-carrid INTO DATA(ls_group_key).
      APPEND VALUE ty_carrier_count( carrid = ls_group_key-carrid
                                     count  = GROUP SIZE ) TO rt_counts.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_carrier_flight_counts_collect.
    DATA lt_sflights TYPE ty_t_sflight.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsocc
      FROM sflight
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights
      UP TO 100 ROWS.

    DATA ls_collect_line TYPE ty_carrier_count.
    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_flight).
      ls_collect_line-carrid = ls_flight-carrid.
      ls_collect_line-count = 1. " Initialize count for COLLECT
      COLLECT ls_collect_line INTO rt_counts.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_modern_counts FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_collect_counts FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_comparison FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_modern_counts.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_grp_010( ).
    DATA(lt_counts) = lo_cut->get_carrier_flight_counts( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lt_counts ).
    LOOP AT lt_counts INTO DATA(ls_entry).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( ls_entry-count > 0 ).
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_collect_counts.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_grp_010( ).
    DATA(lt_counts) = lo_cut->get_carrier_flight_counts_collect( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lt_counts ).
    LOOP AT lt_counts INTO DATA(ls_entry).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( ls_entry-count > 0 ).
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_comparison.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_grp_010( ).
    DATA(lt_modern_counts) = lo_cut->get_carrier_flight_counts( ).
    DATA(lt_collect_counts) = lo_cut->get_carrier_flight_counts_collect( ).

    SORT lt_modern_counts BY carrid.
    SORT lt_collect_counts BY carrid.

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_modern_counts exp = lt_collect_counts ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel vergleicht die moderne `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY` Syntax mit der traditionellen `COLLECT` Anweisung zur Aggregation. Während `COLLECT` weiterhin gültig ist, bietet `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY` eine flexiblere und oft lesbarere Möglichkeit, Gruppierungen und Aggregationen durchzuführen, insbesondere wenn komplexere Logik innerhalb der Gruppen erforderlich ist. Die moderne Variante ist deklarativer und besser in den Fluss der neuen ABAP-Syntax integriert.
keywords: LOOP AT, GROUP BY, GROUP SIZE, COLLECT, Data Aggregation, Internal Tables, Comparison

Instructions: ABAP unterstützt keine statischen abstrakten Methoden direkt. Simulieren Sie dieses Verhalten, indem Sie eine abstrakte Klasse mit einer abstrakten Instanzmethode erstellen, die von einer statischen Methode in einer Hilfsklasse aufgerufen wird, welche die konkrete Implementierung erwartet.
hint: Verwenden Sie ein Interface oder eine abstrakte Klasse mit einer Instanzmethode, die von einer statischen Methode über Polymorphie aufgerufen wird.
solution:
INTERFACE zif_process_step_abs.
  METHODS execute_step RETURNING VALUE(rv_result) TYPE string.
ENDINTERFACE.

CLASS zcl_static_processor DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS METHODS process_all_steps IMPORTING it_steps TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF REF TO zif_process_step_abs
                                    RETURNING VALUE(rt_results) TYPE string_table.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_static_processor IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD process_all_steps.
    LOOP AT it_steps INTO DATA(lo_step).
      APPEND lo_step->execute_step( ) TO rt_results.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_step_a DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_process_step_abs.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_step_a IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_process_step_abs~execute_step.
    rv_result = 'Step A executed'.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_step_b DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES zif_process_step_abs.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_step_b IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD zif_process_step_abs~execute_step.
    rv_result = 'Step B executed'.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_static_processing FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_static_processing.
    DATA lt_steps TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF REF TO zif_process_step_abs.
    APPEND NEW zcl_step_a( ) TO lt_steps.
    APPEND NEW zcl_step_b( ) TO lt_steps.

    DATA(lt_results) = zcl_static_processor=>process_all_steps( it_steps ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lines( lt_results ) exp = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_results[1] exp = 'Step A executed' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lt_results[2] exp = 'Step B executed' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Da ABAP keine statischen abstrakten Methoden unterstützt, kann man dieses Verhalten durch die Verwendung von Interfaces und Polymorphie simulieren. Eine statische Methode kann eine Liste von Objekten verarbeiten, die ein bestimmtes Interface implementieren, und deren Instanzmethoden aufrufen, wodurch ein ähnlicher Effekt wie bei statischen abstrakten Methoden erzielt wird.
keywords: ABSTRACT, Static Method (simulated), Interface, Polymorphism, Object Orientation

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine abstrakte Basisklasse `ZCL_VALIDATOR_ABS` mit einer abstrakten Methode `validate` und einer konkreten Methode `get_error_message`. Implementieren Sie konkrete Validatoren für verschiedene Datentypen (z.B. `ZCL_EMAIL_VALIDATOR`, `ZCL_NUMBER_VALIDATOR`).
hint: Die `validate`-Methode sollte einen booleschen Wert zurückgeben. Die Fehlermeldung wird in einem geschützten Attribut gespeichert.
solution:
CLASS zcl_validator_abs DEFINITION ABSTRACT PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS validate ABSTRACT IMPORTING iv_value TYPE string RETURNING VALUE(rv_is_valid) TYPE abap_bool.
    METHODS get_error_message RETURNING VALUE(rv_message) TYPE string.
  PROTECTED SECTION.
    DATA mv_error_message TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_validator_abs IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_error_message.
    rv_message = mv_error_message.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_email_validator DEFINITION INHERITING FROM zcl_validator_abs PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS validate REDEFINITION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_email_validator IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD validate.
    " Simple email validation regex
    FIND REGEX '^\S+@\S+\.\S+$' IN iv_value.
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      rv_is_valid = abap_true.
      mv_error_message = ''.
    ELSE.
      rv_is_valid = abap_false.
      mv_error_message = 'Invalid email format'.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_number_validator DEFINITION INHERITING FROM zcl_validator_abs PUBLIC FINAL.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS validate REDEFINITION.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_number_validator IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD validate.
    " Check if string contains only digits
    FIND REGEX '^\d+$' IN iv_value.
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      rv_is_valid = abap_true.
      mv_error_message = ''.
    ELSE.
      rv_is_valid = abap_false.
      mv_error_message = 'Value is not a valid number'.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_email_validator FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_number_validator FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_email_validator.
    DATA(lo_email_validator) = NEW zcl_email_validator( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( lo_email_validator->validate( 'test@example.com' ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_false( lo_email_validator->validate( 'invalid-email' ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_email_validator->get_error_message( ) exp = 'Invalid email format' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_number_validator.
    DATA(lo_number_validator) = NEW zcl_number_validator( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( lo_number_validator->validate( '12345' ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_false( lo_number_validator->validate( 'abc' ) ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_number_validator->get_error_message( ) exp = 'Value is not a valid number' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

explanation: Abstrakte Klassen eignen sich hervorragend, um eine gemeinsame Basis für eine Familie von Validatoren zu schaffen. Die abstrakte `validate`-Methode erzwingt, dass jede konkrete Unterklasse ihre eigene Validierungslogik bereitstellt, während gemeinsame Funktionen wie die Fehlerbehandlung in der Basisklasse verbleiben können.
keywords: ABSTRACT, Validation, Object Orientation, Regex

Instructions: Implementieren Sie das Strategy Pattern mit einer abstrakten Basisklasse für Berechnungsstrategien. Erstellen Sie eine abstrakte Klasse `ZCL_CALC_STRATEGY_ABS` mit einer abstrakten Methode `calculate`. Implementieren Sie konkrete Strategien für Addition und Multiplikation.
hint: Die Kontextklasse hält eine Referenz auf die Strategie. Die abstrakte Methode `calculate` wird in den konkreten Strategien implementiert.
solution:
CLASS zcl_calc_strategy_abs DEFINITION ABSTRACT PUBLIC.
